topics: Integration options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-11-18 16:00 PST — Duration: 48 minutes — Recorded via Zoom
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kumar (Redwood SE), Tom Briggs (Redwood SE), Dana Ortiz (Solaris Head of Partnerships), Ola Petrov (Solaris VP Cloud Eng), Mei Lin (Solaris Solutions Architect), Raj Khatri (Solaris BizDev), Kofi Mensah (Solaris Security)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex Chen, AE at Redwood, and with me is Priya our solutions engineer and Tom who's helping on integration patterns. Dana, thanks for coordinating this from Solaris.
[00:17] Dana: Yeah hi thanks, really excited. We're looking to formalize a channel partnership and also evaluate how we can integrate Redwood's inference runtime into some Solaris managed offerings.
[00:34] Priya: Great, quick agenda, we'll do intros, partner program highlights, then dig into technical ways to integrate — hosted API, Redwood Dedicated or Private VPC — and then leave time for questions and next steps.
[00:47] Ola: Sounds good. High level, our infra runs across multiple cloud providers and we also have an edge offering where we co-locate inference hardware in customer sites. So we care about portability and a consistent runtime surface.
[01:03] Priya: Perfect, that's exactly where Redwood aims to help. For partners we typically support three paths: 1) pass-through hosted API with partner billing, 2) Dedicated capacity where you reserve GPU pools for Solaris-managed tenants, and 3) Private deployment where you run Redwood control plane in your VPC or on-prem.
[01:21] Raj: Quick Q — how hard is it to run the private deployment? Our ops team is... well they want something that doesn't feel too bespoke.
[01:32] Tom: Totally. The private deploy comes as a packaged bundle; typical install is Terraform + Helm charts, we provide a reference manifest. Ops work depends on scale — single-cluster pilot is straightforward, multisite edge is more involved. There are known gotchas around nvlink and driver versions, and we have a compatibility matrix we'll share.
[01:50] Mei: Can you share that matrix? Specifics like CUDA versions, MPS vs MIG, and tensor core support matter to us.
[02:02] Priya: Yep — we'll send the compatibility matrix. For edge nodes we support both MIG and multi-instance GPUs; we recommend quantized runtimes for constrained hardware.
[02:16] Dana: From partnership side we care about go-to-market: co-marketing, lead referrals, revenue split. Is that standard across partners or negotiable?
[02:27] Alex: We have a baseline partner program with tiers (registered / gold / strategic). Revenue splits and co-sell commitments are flexible for strategic partners. We'll include the program deck and sample SOW.
[02:41] Ola: On SLAs — if Solaris resells to an enterprise, what do you offer for uptime and latency? Also are there regional controls for data residency?
[02:52] Priya: For hosted API we have region-aware endpoints and SLAs. Dedicated comes with separate SLA (higher uptime guarantees). For Private deployments you control residency entirely and we can provide enterprise support add-ons.
[03:06] Kofi: Security checklist — do you integrate with customer KMS or HSMs? How do you handle tokenization and logs?
[03:15] Priya: We integrate with major KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and support HSM via standard APIs. Audit logs are exportable; we also support token-level encryption for at-rest and in-transit. We'll share our security whitepaper and SOC2 artifact summary.
[03:31] Kofi: Good — we'll need to see those artifacts before any pilot.
[03:36] Alex: Absolutely. We'll add that to next steps.
[03:40] [05:00] Speaker 1: Sorry jumped ahead but a quick thing on cost — for Dedicated what's the typical cost curve, e.g., per-GPU per-hour vs Hosted per-token?
[05:12] Priya: Hosted pricing is per-token and per-embedding unit; Dedicated is a reserved capacity model with monthly commit plus a smaller per-token usage. The break-even depends on token volume and sequence lengths — we can run economic modeling once we see Solarises traffic profile.
[05:33] Mei: We'll share token estimates. Also, can Redwood's runtime be pinned to specific model versions? We often need deterministic outputs for customers.
[05:44] Tom: Yes, model pinning and rollout policies are supported — canary, A/B, automatic fallback to lower-cost variants when capacity constrained.
[05:54] Dana: On the tech integration, we also want to understand if we can surface Redwood capabilities in our self-serve portal. Is there a reseller API?
[06:05] Alex: There is an integrations layer — partner API and SDK that allow provisioning per-customer endpoints, quota management, and billing hooks. We'll share docs for that.
[06:17] Ola: How about benchmarking? We want to run a comparative bench against our current stack (we're using Lambda Labs and some DGX in the cloud). Any recommended approach?
[06:28] Priya: Typical approach: pick 3 representative models, run p99 latency and throughput at target sequence lengths, run quantized vs fp16 variants. We provide a benchmark checklist and tooling; we also can run an assisted benchmark on dedicated infra if Solaris wants — that helps tune kernels and batching.
[06:44] Raj: Do you have references for previous partner benchmarks?
[06:48] Priya: We have a partner case study with a retail customer where we reduced token cost by 28% with batching and KV cache; will link.
[06:55] [08:10] Dana: A couple of tricky questions we get from customers: 1) data residency, 2) auditability for regulated workloads, 3) privacy controls. Can Redwood support per-tenant data retention policies?
[08:26] Priya: Yes — per-tenant retention, masking, and redact-on-write policies are supported in Dedicated and Private deployments. Hosted has configurable retention windows and enterprise add-on for bespoke retention.
[08:40] Kofi: About logs — do you store prompt contents in logs? We need options to not keep PII.
[08:47] Tom: We can disable transcript retention or push logs to customer's SIEM; PII masking can be configured. We'll document the exact toggles.
[08:58] Ola: Integration with SSO? SAML/SCIM?
[09:03] Priya: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. Role-based access controls are included.
[09:10] Mei: Great. Thinking about pilot scope — we imagine doing a pilot with one enterprise customer for 6 weeks, covering chat and embeddings. What's a normal pilot deliverable set?
[09:22] Alex: Pilot deliverables usually include: integration guide, shared benchmark results, runbook for failover, and a recommended production launch plan. Also success criteria — latency p99 < 600ms for chat, cost per 1k tokens below X for embeddings, etc.
[09:41] [11:00] Dana: On commercial terms — do you have partner-resale contracts or do we invoice through Redwood and get referral credit?
[11:09] Alex: Both models available. For strategic partners we frequently do co-sell and co-billing. We'll include sample contracts in the deck.
[11:20] Raj: One more technical — how do you handle KV cache and prefix caching when you do multi-tenant on the same GPU? Concerned about cross-tenant contamination and cache eviction policies.
[11:35] Priya: Good question — KV cache is namespace-isolated per tenant; eviction is workload-aware but respects tenant isolation. For Dedicated we can allocate separate GPU pools per tenant to avoid any noisy neighbor issues.
[11:50] Ola: Are there any constraints around model types? Llama-family, transformer-based, mixture-of-experts?
[11:58] Tom: We support mainstream transformer architectures; MoE can be supported depending on the model's runtime requirements — might need custom kernel paths. We'll need to review specific model forks.
[12:12] [13:30] Dana: On the go-to-market, would Redwood do joint webinars and reference customers?
[13:38] Alex: Yes, joint webinars, case studies, and we often co-host events for strategic partners. We have MDF options for Gold partners.
[13:48] Kofi: Any pre-reqs from security to enter into a pilot? Pen tests, SOC2?
[13:55] Priya: For enterprise pilots we usually request a security questionnaire and provide SOC2 Type II summary. If required we can do an ATO package for federal/regulated workloads.
[14:08] Mei: For the benchmarking session — can Redwood run a controlled bench on your Dedicated infra to compare latency and cost?
[14:15] Priya: Yes, either we can run assisted bench or provide bench scripts for Solaris to run. Assisted bench requires access to a representative dataset and infra.
[14:26] Raj: If we do assisted bench, what's the turnaround?
[14:29] Priya: Typically 7–10 business days from infra access and artifact handoff.
[14:35] [16:00] Speaker 2: There's a question — on network egress costs, if we run Dedicated across regions, how does Redwood surface that to customers?
[16:12] Alex: We expose token-level cost breakdown and per-route cost analytics in the Console; for cross-region egress we include that in the cost modeling and can set routing policies to prefer cheaper regions or provide fallbacks.
[16:26] Ola: That helps. Another item — does Redwood support on-prem air-gapped installs for defense/regulatory customers?
[16:34] Tom: Yes, we offer an on-prem package for air-gapped environments; control plane can be run locally with optional out-of-band licensing. We'll share the installer notes.
[16:47] [18:00] Dana: I'm hearing a number of tangible docs we'll need: partner deck, program terms, benchmark checklist, security whitepaper, install/compat matrix, sample SOW. Can you list those in the follow-up?
[18:12] Alex: We'll include all of those. I'll create a single shared folder and drop the artifacts.
[18:18] Mei: On observability — does Redwood expose per-route traces and token-level latency breakdowns? We want to surface that in our portal for customers.
[18:26] Priya: Yes, Console has token-level cost and latency breakdown, per-model dashboards, and tracing hooks you can export. There are APIs to pull those metrics for embedding in partner portals.
[18:37] Raj: Any gotchas for edge/low-latency customers?
[18:42] Tom: For edge, careful about sequence length and batch size trade-offs. We recommend shorter sequences and aggressive prefix caching. Also pay attention to GPU memory fragmentation — our runtime has optimizations but still will need tuning.
[18:55] [20:00] Kofi: Follow-up from security — does Redwood support customer-managed keys for model weights encryption?
[20:06] Priya: We have KMS integrations; for full model weights encryption you'll want Private or on-prem deployments and we can integrate HSM-backed keys. Hosted API doesn't support customer-managed weight encryption at the moment.
[20:20] Dana: Okay makes sense.
[20:24] Alex: Quick recap, I'll summarize: 1) Alex to send partner deck + sample SOW + contracts and security whitepaper. 2) Priya to send compat matrix, benchmark checklist, and assisted bench options. 3) Solaris to share infra diagram and expected traffic. 4) Schedule technical deep dive in week of 11/24. Anything to add?
[20:44] Mei: Please include requirements for air-gapped install if possible in the SOW appendix.
[20:49] Alex: Will do.
[20:51] [22:00] Dana: Good call — excited to move fast.
[22:04] Alex: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the folder and proposed times.
[22:08] [End of recording — Zoom auto stop]
